value.name: From modules to durable architecture
value.summary: Explore the canonical repository model, its local readers, and the history behind each accepted change.

value.title: One model, several readers
value.narrative: The CLI, server, and browser use one canonical architecture model. The files describe modules and relationships. Each reader chooses what to show without copying that meaning.

value.title: Open a module
value.narrative: Opening a module changes the scope. Selection, focus, filters, and diagram grammar remain presentation choices. The local reader draws the selected architecture and keeps interaction responsive.

value.title: Propose a change
value.narrative: The shared runtime keeps stable identities across modules and flows. A proposal stores changed fields against an exact baseline. It does not copy the whole system into another board.

value.title: Make the edit durable
value.narrative: The runtime validates the complete intent and signs its checkpoint before changing current files. A journal coordinates installation and recovery. Readers hear the result only after durable completion.

value.title: Draw the chosen reading
value.narrative: The shared renderer measures text, lays out modules, and routes connections. The browser owns interaction. Exported pictures carry an exact recipe for the same reading.

value.title: Explain what the reader selected

value.title: Keep and share exact history
value.narrative: Adoption and shelving keep their decisions in retained history. Exact checkpoints preserve the inputs they explain. Sharing source files and publishing the architecture archive are separate actions.
